sn12.11:1.3: The word _āhāra_ (“fuel”, “food”, “nutriment”) means literally “intake”, and is etymologically parallel to _upādāna_, “grasping”, “uptake”. Both terms have dual senses, on the one hand denoting fuel or sustenance, and on the other grasping and attachment. That is why at sometimes _āhāra_ is created by craving, just like _upādāna_ in the standard sequence ([mn9:11.5](), [mn38:16.1]()).
